## INFLUENZA ANTIVIRAL THERAPY RECOMMENDATIONS
## Who to Treat:
The decision to treat should be based on clinical symptoms and/or presence of a
high-risk condition and should NOT be delayed until laboratory test results are
available.
It is important to use antiviral drugs early to treat influenza in people who
are very sick with influenza (for example hospitalized people) and people who
are sick with influenza and have a greater chance of getting severe
complications. If a patient is not in a high-risk group or is not hospitalized,
healthcare providers should use clinical judgment to guide treatment decisions.
## People who have a greater chance of serious influenza complications include:
*Adults aged 65 years or older
*Persons who have chronic pulmonary (including
asthma) or cardiovascular (except isolated hypertension), renal, hepatic,
hematologic, metabolic disorders (including diabetes mellitus), neurologic and
neuro-developmental disorders
*Persons who are immunocompromised due to any
cause (including immunosuppression caused by medications or by HIV infection)
*Pregnant women and women up to 2 weeks after the end of pregnancy
*Persons younger than 19 years of age who are receiving long-term aspirin- or
salicylate-containing medications and who might be at risk for experiencing Reye
syndrome after influenza virus infection *Residents of nursing homes and other
long-term care facilities
*Non-Hispanic Black persons, Hispanic or Latino persons, and American Indian or
Alaska Native persons
*Persons who are extremely obese (BMI greater than or equal to 40)
## Antiviral Treatment:
If indicated, antivirals should be started as soon as possible. Maximal benefit
occurs when treatment is started within 48 hours of symptom onset. However,
antivirals should not be withheld if symptoms begin more than 48 hours prior and
the patient meets criteria for treatment and remains severely ill.
## Treatment Dosing:
Zanamivir is not recommended for patients with chronic respiratory diseases such
as asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. These patients may have
bronchospasm with zanamivir. If zanamivir must be used, and patients are using
an inhaled bronchodilator, zanamivir should be taken just after the
bronchodilator.
Extending the duration of treatment for oseltamivir or peramivir may be needed
for those patients with prolonged illness or who are immunosuppressed.
## Preferred:
Oseltamivir 75 mg po bid [R] for 5 days

Peramivir may not be available. Contact ID for more information.

Hospitalized, high risk:

Acute, uncomplicated:
Peramivir 600mg IV Once [R]
